history.title: Massachusetts enacts first-in-nation transitional bilingual education mandate (Ch. 1005 of the Acts of 1971)
history.description: An Act Providing for the Equal Educational Opportunities of Children with Limited Speaking Ability of the English Language (codified at M.G.L. c. 71A) required districts enrolling 20 or more students of the same non-English language background to provide transitional bilingual education (TBE) in that language. Massachusetts was the first U.S. state to mandate bilingual instruction; the statute became the template cited in the federal Bilingual Education Act's later reauthorizations and in subsequent state TBE laws.

history.title: Voters pass Question 2 — English-only mandate replaces TBE (Ch. 386 of the Acts of 2002)
history.description: Ballot Question 2 ("English Language Education in Public Schools"), modeled on California Proposition 227 (1998) and Arizona Proposition 203 (2000) and bankrolled by Ron Unz's English for the Children campaign, passed roughly 68%–32%. It rewrote M.G.L. c. 71A to repeal the 1971 transitional-bilingual mandate and require Sheltered English Immersion (SEI) for nearly all EL students, with narrowly drawn parental waivers. Effective for the 2003-2004 school year. The mandate remained in force until partially repealed by the 2017 LOOK Act, which restored district choice over program model.

history.title: U.S. DOJ / MA DESE settlement triggers RETELL and the SEI endorsement framework
history.description: Following a federal investigation that found Massachusetts's pre-existing "Category 1-4" SEI training out of compliance with the Equal Educational Opportunities Act and the Castañeda v. Pickard standard, the U.S. Department of Justice and MA DESE entered a settlement agreement. DESE responded by launching RETELL (Rethinking Equity and Teaching for English Language Learners) in 2012 — a statewide initiative that promulgated 603 CMR 7.14(1), the Sheltered English Immersion endorsement, and required core-academic teachers and administrators of ELs to obtain it on a phased schedule. RETELL is the operational backbone the LOOK Act later codified.

history.title: Massachusetts enacts the LOOK Act (Ch. 138 of the Acts of 2017)
history.description: An Act Relative to Language Opportunity for Our Kids (LOOK Act) repealed the 2002 English-only mandate and authorized districts to choose program models including dual language, two-way immersion, transitional bilingual, SEI, and other research-based approaches. The act also authorized the State Seal of Biliteracy and codified the SEI endorsement framework binding core-academic teachers of ELs (later operationalized at 603 CMR 7.14(1)).

history.title: Massachusetts authorizes State Seal of Biliteracy
history.description: The LOOK Act simultaneously authorized the Massachusetts State Seal of Biliteracy. DESE administers the credential for high-school graduates demonstrating proficiency in English plus one or more world languages.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Massachusetts's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: SEI endorsement requirement extended to vocational educators
history.description: Effective 2021-07-01, MA DESE extended the SEI endorsement requirement (already binding on core-academic teachers and administrators of ELs) to vocational educators serving ELs. This expanded the operative scope of `sei.mandatedForAllTeachers = true` in MA without changing the underlying coding.
